newsitem.title: ANGOLA: U.N. in Angola sends report on UNITA to Annan.
newsitem.headline: U.N. in Angola sends report on UNITA to Annan.

text.p: The United Nations in Angola said on Friday it was no longer waiting for a response from former rebel movement UNITA and had already sent a report to Secretary General Kofi Annan on whether sanctions should be imposed.
On June 30 the U.N. Security Council gave the former rebels until Friday August 15 to reply to demands to comply with the country's long peace process or risk facing sanctions.
UNITA was told to list its armed men, start handing over territory to the government and make its radio station non-partisan.
Sanctions for failing to do so would include a ban on foreign travel by UNITA members and curbs on banking, including a possible freeze on bank accounts.
U.N. Observer mission spokesman David Wimhurst told Reuters on Friday, "We are not now waiting for a UNITA response. The report has already been sent to New York."
Barring any last minute UNITA proposals, the U.N. statement points toward sanctions, diplomats say.
"If UNITA does not come up with something a lot better before the Security Council convenes," said one western diplomat, "then they are going to get hit with sanctions."
UNITA replied last week. Details were not made public but the U.N. mission here, comprising observers from the United States, Portugal and Russia, said that response was inadequate.

Wimhurst's comment dampened the chances that UNITA, which fought the former Marxist government for two decades until 1994 -- at times with U.S. and white South African support -- could influence the U.N. decision by a second, last-minute response.
U.N. officials and diplomats in Luanda say that even though the deadline for the report is Friday the Security Council will probably not sit to discuss the matter until next week.

Senior UNITA members in Luanda said on Thursday that UNITA's chief representative to the peace process, Isaias Samakuva, would return to Luanda on Friday after consultations with UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi in his highland headquarters of Bailundo.
"It is likely Ambassador Samakuva will bring some more information for the United Nations when he arrives on Friday," said one UNITA official.
